CS 409 / CS 509

Ethical Hacking

  • Undergraduate and graduate
  • 3 credits

Offered: Fall 2026, Fall 2025, Fall 2024

Students examine how security weaknesses arise in computing systems and how to recognize, assess, and address them. Lectures and controlled virtual-machine labs connect security principles to defensive decisions and responsible professional practice.

Selected Topics

  • Cybersecurity foundations, authentication, and privacy
  • Network, system, web, and database security
  • Malware and social engineering risks
  • Firewalls, intrusion detection, and network protection

Learning Objectives

  • Assess security weaknesses and propose safeguards for a given network scenario.
  • Explain how security controls reduce risk and when to use them.
  • Develop and communicate a network protection plan.

Coursework & Projects

Assignments, controlled labs, quizzes, and exams build applied security judgment. CS 509 students also complete a graduate research project, communicating their findings through a technical report, an oral presentation, or both.
